summary: Telegram-controlled remote shell backdoor with command obfuscation
details: httpz-requests ships a Telegram bot that connects out to the Telegram Bot API, receives messages from an allow-listed owner ID, and executes their contents as shell commands on the host running the CLI (entry point httpz-requests = httpz_requests.cli:main; __init__.py imports start_bot from.bot). This is a network->shell dataflow: a remote party holding the bot token and owner ID gets arbitrary command execution on the machine running the tool. The package additionally ships a compiled Cython obfuscate module (httpz_requests/obfuscate.cpython-312-x86_64-linux-gnu.so); the README states that commands are encoded prior to execution so the plaintext does not appear in process listings or logs, layering anti-forensics onto the remote-shell capability. Publisher metadata is unfilled template values (Author-email 'you@example.com', Project-URL pointing at 'YOUR_GITHUB_USERNAME'), so there is no identifiable maintainer behind the remote-code-execution capability, and the shell/bot logic is shipped as compiled.so modules rather than reviewable source.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
